# _autosummary/coact.synthesis.html.md

# coact.synthesis

Persona & return-contract synthesis — the two real “extras” of a skill→agent lift.

COACT_SPEC §5.5 / §3.2. A skill body is *procedural*, not a persona, and skills
return *nothing*. The two fields that actually turn a skill into an agent are the
**system prompt (persona/identity)** and the \*\*return contract (consumable
output)\*\*. This module synthesizes both.

This PR ships the **template** path (no LLM, always available, a sound default).
The optional **LLM-assisted** path (a richer persona drafted from the skill body
via an injected facade) is added on top in a later milestone — both paths obey
the same rules: author-pinned `coact: persona` / `coact: returns` always win
(inspectable, overridable, LLM-assisted-but-not-required, DECISIONS D10).

Crucially the persona **references** the skill by name and instructs the agent to
follow it — it never copies the skill body (point-don’t-copy / SSOT, §3.3).

### Module Attributes

| [`DEFAULT_RETURN_SCHEMA`](_autosummary/coact.synthesis.html.md#coact.synthesis.DEFAULT_RETURN_SCHEMA)   | A generic-but-useful default return schema (used when the author pins none).   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`render_return_contract_section`](_autosummary/coact.synthesis.html.md#coact.synthesis.render_return_contract_section)(rc)                | Render the human/model-facing "Return contract" markdown for a persona body.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`synthesize_persona`](_autosummary/coact.synthesis.html.md#coact.synthesis.synthesize_persona)(skill, \*, return_contract)    | Synthesize the system prompt (persona) for an agent derived from `skill`.      |
| [`synthesize_return_contract`](_autosummary/coact.synthesis.html.md#coact.synthesis.synthesize_return_contract)(skill, \*, coact_meta) | Choose the agent's return contract: author-pinned, else a template default.    |

### coact.synthesis.DEFAULT_RETURN_SCHEMA *= {'properties': {'result': {'description': 'The primary artifact or finding.'}, 'status': {'enum': ['ok', 'partial', 'failed'], 'type': 'string'}, 'summary': {'description': 'One-paragraph summary of what was done.', 'type': 'string'}}, 'required': ['summary', 'status'], 'type': 'object'}*

A generic-but-useful default return schema (used when the author pins none).

### coact.synthesis.render_return_contract_section(rc)

Render the human/model-facing “Return contract” markdown for a persona body.

```pycon
>>> rc = ReturnContract(json_schema={'type': 'object'}, description='findings')
>>> 'Return contract' in render_return_contract_section(rc)
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### coact.synthesis.synthesize_persona(skill, , return_contract, tools=None, extra_skills=None, llm=None)

Synthesize the system prompt (persona) for an agent derived from `skill`.

Wraps the skill’s intent as an identity, states operating invariants, and
appends the return contract — while **pointing at** the source skill rather
than inlining it (§3.3). The identity paragraph is template-generated by
default; when an `llm` is resolvable it is *drafted* by the LLM instead
(richer, but the invariants and the return contract stay deterministic so the
machine-facing contract is never at the mercy of generation). The LLM is
optional — absent one, the template path is a sound default (DECISIONS D10).

```pycon
>>> from skill.base import Skill, SkillMeta
>>> s = Skill(meta=SkillMeta(name='ux-analyst', description='Analyze UX bundles.'), body='steps')
>>> rc = ReturnContract(json_schema={'type': 'object'}, description='findings')
>>> persona, src = synthesize_persona(s, return_contract=rc, tools=['Read', 'Grep'])
>>> 'ux-analyst' in persona and 'Return contract' in persona and src == 'synthesized-template'
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[`'skill'`, `'coact-frontmatter'`, `'policy'`, `'inferred'`, `'synthesized-template'`, `'synthesized-llm'`, `'default'`]]

### coact.synthesis.synthesize_return_contract(skill, , coact_meta)

Choose the agent’s return contract: author-pinned, else a template default.

```pycon
>>> from skill.base import Skill, SkillMeta
>>> s = Skill(meta=SkillMeta(name='x', description='y'), body='z')
>>> rc, src = synthesize_return_contract(s, coact_meta=CoactMeta())
>>> rc.json_schema['type'], src
('object', 'synthesized-template')
>>> rc2, src2 = synthesize_return_contract(s, coact_meta=CoactMeta(returns={'schema_ref': 'm:N'}))
>>> rc2.ref, src2
('m:N', 'coact-frontmatter')
```

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`ReturnContract`](_autosummary/coact.base.html.md#coact.base.ReturnContract), [`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[`'skill'`, `'coact-frontmatter'`, `'policy'`, `'inferred'`, `'synthesized-template'`, `'synthesized-llm'`, `'default'`]]


# _autosummary/coact.util.html.md

# coact.util

Pure helpers for coact with no internal coact imports.

Small, reusable string/name utilities and a thin `check_requirements` helper
for the optional-dependency backends (Agent SDK, py2mcp/FastMCP, an LLM
provider). Kept dependency-free so every other coact module can import it.

### Functions

| [`agent_filename`](_autosummary/coact.util.html.md#coact.util.agent_filename)(name)                     | Return the safe `<name>.md` filename for an agent, rejecting unsafe names.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`check_requirements`](_autosummary/coact.util.html.md#coact.util.check_requirements)(modules, \*, feature) | Verify optional dependencies are importable, else raise an actionable error. |
| [`first_balanced_span`](_autosummary/coact.util.html.md#coact.util.first_balanced_span)(s[, opener, closer]) | Return the first depth-balanced `opener…closer` substring of `s`.            |
| [`import_object`](_autosummary/coact.util.html.md#coact.util.import_object)(ref)                       | Resolve a `'module.path:attr'` or `'module.path.attr'` reference.            |
| [`safe_filename`](_autosummary/coact.util.html.md#coact.util.safe_filename)(name, \*[, suffix, kind])  | Return `f"{name}{suffix}"` after rejecting unsafe, path-bearing names.       |
| [`to_kebab_case`](_autosummary/coact.util.html.md#coact.util.to_kebab_case)(name)                      | Convert CamelCase / snake_case / spaces to kebab-case.                       |
| [`to_snake_case`](_autosummary/coact.util.html.md#coact.util.to_snake_case)(name)                      | Convert CamelCase / kebab-case / spaces to snake_case.                       |

### coact.util.agent_filename(name)

Return the safe `<name>.md` filename for an agent, rejecting unsafe names.

Agent names become files under `.claude/agents/`; a name carrying a path
separator or `..` could escape that directory (CWE-22 path traversal) on
write *or* read. Names must be a bare filename stem. Raises `ValueError` on
an empty, non-string, or path-bearing name — the check lives at the
filesystem boundary so in-memory [`AgentDefinition`](_autosummary/coact.base.html.md#coact.base.AgentDefinition)s stay
unconstrained.

```pycon
>>> agent_filename('ux-analyst')
'ux-analyst.md'
>>> agent_filename('../escape')
Traceback (most recent call last):
    ...
ValueError: unsafe agent name '../escape': ...
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### coact.util.check_requirements(modules, , feature)

Verify optional dependencies are importable, else raise an actionable error.

`modules` maps an importable module name to the pip target that provides
it (e.g. `{'claude_agent_sdk': 'claude-agent-sdk'}`). Raises
`ImportError` listing the exact `pip install` line for whatever is
missing — and, when some requirements *are* present, which ones — the
package-UX convention for optional backends (informative, actionable errors).

```pycon
>>> check_requirements({'json': 'json'}, feature='noop')  # importable -> no raise
```

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### coact.util.first_balanced_span(s, opener='{', closer='}')

Return the first depth-balanced `opener…closer` substring of `s`.

Brackets inside double-quoted JSON strings are ignored, so a valid value
followed by prose that itself contains brackets is not over-captured (a
greedy `opener.*closer` would run to the *last* `closer` and fail to
parse). Returns `None` when no balanced span starts in `s`. Shared by the
LLM-reply JSON extractors ([`coact.llm`](_autosummary/coact.llm.html.md#module-coact.llm), [`coact.realize_litellm`](_autosummary/coact.html.md#coact.realize_litellm)).

```pycon
>>> first_balanced_span('Result: {"a": 1}. Note: {braces}.')
'{"a": 1}'
>>> first_balanced_span('see [1, [2, 3]] end', '[', ']')
'[1, [2, 3]]'
>>> first_balanced_span('no brackets here') is None
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### coact.util.import_object(ref)

Resolve a `'module.path:attr'` or `'module.path.attr'` reference.

Prefer the `module:attr` form (unambiguous). Falls back to splitting on the
last dot for the dotted form.

```pycon
>>> import_object('json:dumps')
<function dumps at ...>
>>> import_object('os.path.join')
<function join at ...>
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

### coact.util.safe_filename(name, , suffix='', kind='name')

Return `f"{name}{suffix}"` after rejecting unsafe, path-bearing names.

Names that become files must be bare filename stems; one carrying a path
separator or `..` could escape its directory (CWE-22) on write *or* read.
Raises `ValueError` on an empty, non-string, or path-bearing name. `kind`
customizes the error wording for the caller’s domain. Shared by
[`agent_filename()`](_autosummary/coact.util.html.md#coact.util.agent_filename) (`.md` agents) and the publish axis (`.mcpb` bundles).

```pycon
>>> safe_filename('paths', suffix='.mcpb')
'paths.mcpb'
>>> safe_filename('../x', suffix='.mcpb')
Traceback (most recent call last):
    ...
ValueError: unsafe name '../x': ...
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### coact.util.to_kebab_case(name)

Convert CamelCase / snake_case / spaces to kebab-case.

```pycon
>>> to_kebab_case('UxAnalyst')
'ux-analyst'
>>> to_kebab_case('ux_analyst')
'ux-analyst'
>>> to_kebab_case('already-kebab')
'already-kebab'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### coact.util.to_snake_case(name)

Convert CamelCase / kebab-case / spaces to snake_case.

```pycon
>>> to_snake_case('UxAnalyst')
'ux_analyst'
>>> to_snake_case('ux-analyst')
'ux_analyst'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

# ai-agents.html.md

<!-- generated by epythet -->

# For AI agents

`coact` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `ai-assistant-agent-runtime`

Use this skill whenever the user wants to add, refactor, or audit the agent runtime — the loop that drives multi-step tool-using LLM conversations, optionally with durable execution for long-running, resumable agents. Triggers include “add an agent loop”, “make my agent multi-step”, “stop the agent from looping forever”, “resume an agent after a crash”, “run an agent in the background”, “agent handoff to sub-agent”, “add Pydantic AI / LangGraph / OpenAI Agents SDK”, “wrap my agent in Temporal / DBOS / Inngest / Restate”, “stream agent state to the UI”, “cancel a running agent”, “human-in-the-loop approval mid-run”, or any task on the agent orchestration or durable execution layers. Read BEFORE writing a custom agent loop.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/coact ai-assistant-agent-runtime --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/ai-assistant-agent-runtime`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/coact/tree/HEAD/skills/ai-assistant-agent-runtime).

### `ai-assistant-architect`

Use this skill whenever the user wants to add, audit, refactor, or maintain an embedded AI assistant (chat + agentic) inside their own application. Triggers include phrases like “add an AI assistant to my app”, “wire up a chatbot”, “embed Claude/GPT into my UI”, “make my app operable by AI”, “audit my AI assistant integration”, “what should I add next for my AI assistant”, “let users bring their own AI API keys”, or any task that touches multiple of {chat UI, system prompts, skills, MCP tools, agent runtime, command dispatch → MCP, multi-tenancy, observability, billing} together. This is the entry-point skill — it audits the codebase, identifies the layer in question, and routes to the focused sub-skills (ai-assistant-chat-ui, ai-assistant-prompts-skills, ai-assistant-command-mcp, ai-assistant-agent-runtime).

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/coact ai-assistant-architect --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/ai-assistant-architect`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/coact/tree/HEAD/skills/ai-assistant-architect).

### `ai-assistant-chat-ui`

Use this skill whenever the user wants to add, modify, or audit the chat UI / streaming / wire-protocol layer of an embedded AI assistant. Triggers include “build a chat UI”, “add streaming responses”, “render tool calls in the chat”, “add thread CRUD”, “show markdown in the assistant”, “branch conversations”, “make the AI response copyable”, “switch from polling to streaming”, “embed Claude into my React app”, “set up assistant-ui”, “use Vercel AI SDK in my app”, “expose chat over SSE from FastAPI”, or any task on the frontend chat layer of a React + Vite + shadcn application. Read this skill BEFORE writing any new chat component, runtime hook, or SSE endpoint.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/coact ai-assistant-chat-ui --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/ai-assistant-chat-ui`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/coact/tree/HEAD/skills/ai-assistant-chat-ui).

### `ai-assistant-command-mcp`

Use this skill whenever the user wants to expose application operations to an AI assistant via tools/function-calling/MCP. Triggers include “make my app operable by AI”, “expose my commands to Claude/GPT”, “build an MCP server for my app”, “bridge command dispatch to MCP”, “annotate tools for AI”, “add tool approval flow”, “scope tools per user”, “stop the AI from calling destructive operations without confirmation”, “compose multiple MCP servers”, “use py2mcp”, “use FastMCP”, “use the MCP TypeScript SDK”, or any task that wires application operations to the agent’s tool surface. Look for command dispatch (any of: @command decorator, CommandSpec, acture, wrapex, py2mcp, a registry of typed handlers). If absent, prefer adding one first.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/coact ai-assistant-command-mcp --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/ai-assistant-command-mcp`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/coact/tree/HEAD/skills/ai-assistant-command-mcp).

### `ai-assistant-prompts-skills`

Use this skill whenever the user wants to add, refactor, manage, or audit system prompts, user-editable prompts, or “skills” (Anthropic-style) in an AI assistant. Triggers include “set up a prompt registry”, “version my system prompts”, “add a skill to my assistant”, “make prompts editable by non-engineers”, “auto-select the right skill”, “write a SKILL.md”, “integrate Langfuse for prompt management”, “add prompt evals to CI”, “manage prompt versions”, “load context dynamically per request”, “store prompts in git”, or any task involving the SSOT for instructions an LLM consumes. Read this skill BEFORE creating any prompts/ or skills/ directory or wiring up a prompt store.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/coact ai-assistant-prompts-skills --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/ai-assistant-prompts-skills`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/coact/tree/HEAD/skills/ai-assistant-prompts-skills).

### `coact`

Start here for coact — the package that turns your .claude/skills/ into .claude/agents/ definitions (COMPLETE) and those into running agents (REALIZE), plus tooling to see and move between the layers (diff/estimate/inventory/back) and scaffold a starter fleet. Use when someone asks “how do I use coact”, “what can coact do”, “turn my skills into agents”, “reuse my AI stuff across the agent stack”, or isn’t sure which coact capability they need. Routes to the focused coact-complete / coact-realize / coact-analyze skills.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/coact coact --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/coact`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/coact/tree/HEAD/skills/coact).

### `coact-analyze`

Use when inspecting or moving between the skill/agent layers with coact — auditing what extras an agent adds over its skill, estimating the token cost of fanning out a fleet before you spend it, enumerating a project’s reusable AI assets, or harvesting an agent back into a skill. Triggers on “diff this skill and agent”, “what does this agent add”, “how much will a fleet cost”, “is multi-agent worth it here”, “list the skills/agents/tools in this project”, “inventory”, or “turn this agent back into a skill”.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/coact coact-analyze --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/coact-analyze`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/coact/tree/HEAD/skills/coact-analyze).

### `coact-complete`

Use when turning an existing .claude/skills/ skill into a .claude/agents/ agent definition with coact — i.e. COMPLETE. Triggers on “complete a skill into an agent”, “make an agent from this skill”, “what extras would coact add”, “fill in the coact frontmatter block”, or wanting a dry-run/provenance preview before generating an agent. Covers complete(), plan_completion(), the additive coact frontmatter, and the no-LLM default.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/coact coact-complete --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/coact-complete`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/coact/tree/HEAD/skills/coact-complete).

### `coact-dev`

Use when developing, debugging, reviewing, or extending the coact package itself (this repo) — adding emit targets or realize backends, touching COMPLETE/REALIZE, the additive coact frontmatter, the policy, or the LLM/synthesis paths. Covers the architecture, the invariants that must not be broken, the open-closed extension points, and the testing/tooling gotchas specific to this repo.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/coact coact-dev --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/coact-dev`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/coact/tree/HEAD/skills/coact-dev).

### `coact-publish`

Publish a Python capability as a deployable AI-chatbot integration with coact — package tools (module:function refs, live functions, or a skill’s coact: mcp block) into a Claude Desktop one-click .mcpb extension (a local stdio MCP server). Use when the user wants to create, build, package, or deploy a Claude connector / plugin / MCP server / .mcpb / Desktop Extension / “integration” from existing Python code or a skill — e.g. “make an mcpb”, “package these functions for Claude”, “turn this into a Claude extension/connector”, “publish a local MCP server”, “wrap my tools as a Claude Desktop extension”. Also use to draft an integration from a natural-language description (“describe an integration”, “I want a Claude connector that can…”) via `coact describe`. Also covers REMOTE claude.ai connectors (a hosted Streamable-HTTP MCP server + OAuth 2.1) via the `claude-remote-connector` target — use when the user wants a cloud-reachable connector, not a local install.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/coact coact-publish --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/coact-publish`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/coact/tree/HEAD/skills/coact-publish).

### `coact-realize`

Use when turning a coact agent definition (or a skill) into something that actually runs — i.e. REALIZE. Triggers on “realize this agent”, “run a coact agent”, “materialize an agent for Claude Code”, “make an aw/Agent-SDK runnable from a skill”, “run a definition through LiteLLM/LangGraph/CrewAI”, “expose a skill’s tools as an MCP server”, or choosing between the host/sdk/litellm/langgraph/crewai/mcp backends and their cost. Covers realize(), the backends, install extras, and the fan-out cost gate.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/coact coact-realize --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/coact-realize`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/coact/tree/HEAD/skills/coact-realize).

## Subagents

Subagents are Markdown files with a frontmatter (`name`, `description`, `tools`) and a system prompt as the body. Copy one into your project’s `.claude/agents/` (or your agent host’s equivalent) to delegate the task it describes.

### `coact-docs-checker`

Use to verify coact’s documentation still matches its code — before a release, after an API change, or when README/docstrings/DECISIONS may have drifted. Dispatch to cross-check the README’s Python snippets and CLI commands against real signatures, the install extras against pyproject.toml, DECISIONS.md against the implementation, and that every module has a complete top-level docstring. Returns a list of concrete drift findings, not edits.

Source: [`.claude/agents/coact-docs-checker.md`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/coact/tree/HEAD/.claude/agents/coact-docs-checker.md); tools: `Read, Grep, Glob, Bash`.

### `coact-reviewer`

Use to review a change, diff, or PR to the coact package against its invariants before it lands. Dispatch when code under coact/ has changed and you want a focused correctness + invariant audit (no-LLM mechanical path, lazy SDK import, point-don’t-copy, JSON-Schema return contract, open-closed registries, keyword-only discipline, module docstrings). Returns a structured verdict with file:line findings, not a rewrite.

Source: [`.claude/agents/coact-reviewer.md`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/coact/tree/HEAD/.claude/agents/coact-reviewer.md); tools: `Read, Grep, Glob, Bash`.

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/coact/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`coact.md`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/coact/coact.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/coact/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)


# api.html.md

# API reference

| [`coact`](_autosummary/coact.html.md#module-coact)   | coact — reuse your AI stuff across the layers of the modern agent stack.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
